experiment.question: How much of the seat's damage output comes from the choices, and how much from the aiming controller?
experiment.hypothesis: If the controller does most of the work, random choices through the precision controller will approach the scripted policy through it, and degrading the controller will cost both about equally. If the choices matter, the policy keeps most of its advantage over random under every controller.

interactions.note: The effect of brain (random → script:skirmisher) at control=precision, minus the same effect at control=direct. Far from zero means the two factors do not contribute separately.
The effect of brain (random → script:skirmisher) at motor=standard, minus the same effect at motor=degraded. Far from zero means the two factors do not contribute separately.

contribution.statement: Each contrast is the paired, by-seed difference between two arms that differ in one factor only, at the other factors' stated levels. It is descriptive for this design and this environment. Effects interact, so they are not shares of a whole and do not sum to one.

warnings.message: 3 seeds per arm. Treat every difference as exploratory; use a 10-seed development set or a 30-seed evaluation set before claiming one.
